event_confirmation: Company release, GlobeNewswire 2026-10-20 16:05 EDT, 'Cipher Digital Announces Date of Third Quarter 2026 Business Update Conference Call': results before U.S. markets open Monday 2026-11-02, call and webcast 08:00 ET. Mirrored at https://www.stocktitan.net/news/CIFR/cipher-digital-announces-date-of-third-quarter-2026-business-update-ieebc0f9cvt8.html, and the headline appears in the finviz CIFR news list (https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=CIFR). The window is the 2026-10-30 close to the 2026-11-02 close.
conviction_note: The non-result is close to right here. The Q3 KPIs that lead the business update (contracted revenue of $16.6bn, 907 MW, Black Pearl rent started in August, the Barber Lake hall schedule) were already published in the 2026-10-13 convertible-offering deck. The bar of about $38m revenue and -$0.26 to -$0.31 EPS does not decide this name's reaction; lease news does. What tilts p_up slightly above 50 is positioning: the stock is down 53.6% in 20 days and sits at its 52-week low, 21.7-26.6% of the float is short, and the 25-delta skew is -14.7 (calls bid). That lean agrees with the skew, so it is probably mostly priced, and p_up stays at 54. abs_move is 17, slightly above the 15.9% implied move, because the name moved 12-24% on each of its last three prints. The scaled number (+1.36) and impact_sum (+1.4) agree; neither was fitted to the other.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue of about $38.0m and EPS of -$0.31 (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-10-26, https://finviz.com/news/407867/cipher-minings-first-lease-revenue-faces-a-market-that-has-already-lost-faith). Second source: Chartmill, $38.9m and -$0.26 (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/CIFR/estimates). The two agree on revenue within about 2% and differ on EPS. The company gives no numeric guidance; the Q2 release had no Q3 or Q4 numbers (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1819989/000181998926000038/q226_earningsxprxdraftxvf.htm). Q2 missed: revenue $24.8m against a $31.0m consensus, EPS -$0.65 against -$0.21.
positioning_check: Short float is 26.58%, short ratio 2.32 days, float 344.5m (finviz quote page read 2026-10-30, https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=CIFR). Tapeboard has 21.7% of float as of the 2026-09-30 settlement with 1.7 days to cover, ranked #1 most-shorted on 10-14/10-19/10-20, with a borrow fee of 37.9% on 10-20 that its 10-19 page contradicts at 0.4% (https://tapeboard.com/most-shorted-stocks/2026-10-20). Part of this is likely convert-arbitrage hedging of the new $850m 2032 notes and the remaining 2030 notes, which is mechanical and not squeeze fuel. Baseline skew is -14.74 vol points (25-delta put IV below call IV: upside is paid for), put/call open interest 0.47, event-implied move 15.86%. Run-up is -53.63% over 20 days and -8.25% over 5 days, at the 52-week low and -75% from the high.

findings.finding: The short base is crowded and the stock has capitulated going into the print. Short float is 21.7% (9/30 settlement, 1.7 days to cover) to 26.6% (finviz, 10/30). The stock is -53.6% over 20 days and at its 52-week low, and closed the last pre-print session down about 10-13% on a crypto-equity selloff. Options price upside (25-delta skew -14.7 vol points, put/call open interest 0.47). Any stabilising line on Nov 2 (lease timing held, no new equity) meets a short base that has to cover into a thin bid.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last three prints were +12.48% (2026-02-24), +23.53% (2026-05-05, rose despite a revenue miss on the mining-exit / AI repricing story) and -15.65% (2026-08-04, miss with the lease ramp still distant). Two of three were up, and the up moves were larger than the down move.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the call-side skew already says the options market expects upside convexity. If the squeeze were fully priced, the stock would not be closing at fresh 52-week lows the session before the print, and the skew would not need to sit this far negative. Part of the short interest is convert-arb hedging, which does not cover on news. That is why this is sized small.
findings.independence: Tapeboard most-shorted list, 2026-10-20 (https://tapeboard.com/most-shorted-stocks/2026-10-20), a different provider with a different settlement date. The skew is from the sealed baseline, a separate dataset.

findings.finding: Most of the Q3 business-update headline numbers were pre-published in the 2026-10-13 offering deck (8-K EX-99.1), stated as of 2026-09-30: 907 MW operating and contracted, 700 MW contracted gross HPC, $16.6bn contracted revenue (+46% vs Q2), WALT 17.3 years. The deck also said the first Black Pearl capacity was delivered in August, two months early, with rent started, and that no Barber Lake rent credits had been incurred to date. The reported quarter's KPI surprise is therefore small, and what is new on Nov 2 is Q4 delivery status and any new contract.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-08-04 the market sold the print (-15.65%) on lease-ramp timing rather than the KPIs. On 2026-05-05 it rose 23.5% despite a revenue miss. The KPI line has not been what moves this name.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. It is filed because it shows the reported-quarter KPIs are known, so a beat or miss on them should move the stock little. If it were not priced, the Q3 contracted-revenue figure would still be a pending headline in previews; the Earnings Whispers preview instead frames the print around first lease revenue.
findings.independence: The Black Pearl early delivery and rent start also appear in the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1819989/000181998926000038/q226_earningsxprxdraftxvf.htm).

findings.finding: Barber Lake's first rent has already slipped. The Q2-era plan was the initial 168 MW phase by September 2026, with rent 'from October'. The 2026-09-25 amendment moved to phased delivery: halls 1-2 in Q4 2026, halls 3-4 in Q4 2026 to Q1 2027, hall 5 in Q1 2027. Cipher bears the first $359.3m of overruns, and the deck shows an estimated all-in cost of $2.94-2.97bn against a $2.70-2.72bn original budget. The Nov 2 call is the first chance to say whether halls 1-2 were handed over in October, or whether the schedule slips again.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-08-04 the stock fell -15.65% with coverage headlined 'AI lease ramp stays distant'. Rent timing is the line this name has sold on.
findings.why_not_priced: The slip and the overrun burden have been public since 9-25 and the stock has halved since, so the known part is priced. Only a further slip is unpriced. No source reports a hall delivered in October (searched); management said on 9-25 it 'remains on track'. Sized toward zero because the finding lands inside what the company already told the market.
findings.independence: Datacenterdynamics/finviz coverage of the amendment gives the original 168 MW by September 2026 timeline (https://datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/cipher-extends-barber-lake-data-center-lease-commitments-to-20-years). TIKR 2026-10-22 also lists first Barber Lake rent in Q4 as the next test. Same underlying company disclosure.

findings.finding: Financing, asked what it buys: the $850m 0.00% 2032 converts (conversion price about $15.31, a 35% premium to $11.34) fund about $750m of extra Barber Lake equity behind a $9.1bn contracted lease, plus pipeline build-out. A 45-day company lock-up from 10-13 runs to about late November, so no new equity raise can be announced with the print. The dilution is already done: about 40.7m shares were issued for $165.9m of 2030 notes.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell -12.8% on the 10-13 announcement, -12.3% on pricing day and -10.6% on settlement (TIKR). The financing has been sold hard already.
findings.why_not_priced: The dilution is priced, given -36% since pricing. Not obviously priced is that the print cannot carry an ATM or follow-on, the usual negative tail for a capex-heavy name reporting at its lows. If the market were pricing a print-day raise, put skew would be bid, and it is not.
findings.independence: The lock-up and use of proceeds are from the offering deck (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1819989/000119312526419743/d134900dex991.htm), the same filing. The share count is from TIKR, 2026-10-22 (https://www.tikr.com/blog/cipher-digital-lost-31-in-a-week-cantor-fitzgerald-still-sees-112-upside).

findings.finding: The revenue bar of about $38m (Earnings Whispers 10-26; Chartmill $38.9m) needs roughly +$13m over Q2's $24.8m mining revenue. It rests on two months of Black Pearl rent, while bitcoin mining is being wound down (miners held for sale went from $94.9m to zero in H1). Q2 missed revenue by about 20%, and the company gives no numeric guide. Slight miss risk, print_vs_bar about -3%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 missed revenue and the stock rose +23.5%. Q2 2026 missed revenue ($24.8m vs $31.0m) and EPS and fell -15.65%. The sign came from the lease narrative, not the revenue miss.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar is from consensus, so it is what the market holds. A miss is not visible in the price, but this name's reaction history shows it has not paid on the revenue line, so sized small.

findings.finding: There is probably a large non-cash warrant-liability gain in Q3 GAAP results. In Q2 a rising stock produced a $150.5m warrant fair-value charge that drove EPS to -$0.65. In Q3 the stock fell from about $23-24 at 6/30 (TIKR: -45% from 6/30 to about $13 on 10/10) to about $15.9 at the start of October (Form 4: 10/2 settlement VWAP $15.87). That points to a fair-value gain that could swing headline GAAP EPS above the -$0.26 to -$0.31 consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's $150.5m warrant charge produced a large GAAP miss (-$0.65 vs -$0.21), and coverage called it non-cash. The stock fell on lease timing, not the charge.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of -$0.26 to -$0.31 looks like it excludes the remeasurement, so a headline 'EPS beat' is likely. It is below operating income with no path to the guide, so it is worth a fraction: headline algorithms only.
findings.independence: TIKR, 2026-10-10, for the 6/30-to-10/10 decline (https://www.tikr.com/de/blog/cipher-digital-stock-has-lost-45-since-june-30-heres-why-its-next-lease-matters-more-than-rising-yields). The Q2 release for the warrant mechanics.

findings.finding: The company has a pattern of bundling a lease with its business update. The Q3 2025 update (2025-11-03) came with the AWS 300 MW / $5.5bn lease and the 1 GW Colchis JV. Today Colchis (1 GW, conditional Batch Zero) and Apollo (land secured, 2028 target) are unleased. A Blockspace headline on 10-28 says Morgan Stanley reiterated Overweight on Cipher and four peers, and the same outlet reports MS expecting powered-shell operators to sign a wave of contracts by October. Cipher has signed no new lease since the 9-25 Barber Lake extension. A Colchis or Apollo lease at the print is the upside tail; none is reported.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2025-11-03 Q3 update with the AWS lease announcement surged (247wallst, 'Cipher Mining Surges on Amazon AI Lease Announcement'). The 2026-05-05 update with the mining exit rose +23.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an inference, not a document. If a lease were expected, the stock would not be at 52-week lows with analysts like Cantor cutting targets ($28 to $19). The call skew is the one sign that some upside tail is priced. Sized as a proxy.
findings.independence: Blockspace, Morgan Stanley powered-shell deal wave (https://blockspace.media/insight/morgan-stanley-powered-shell-deal-wave-october/; page returned 403, used from search snippet). The Colchis/Apollo status is from the 10-13 offering deck (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1819989/000119312526419743/d134900dex991.htm).

findings.finding: The 10%-holder Bitfury/V3 is delivering pledged shares under variable prepaid forwards struck in Nov 2025, all at the floor because price is under about $21.4: 1.84m shares on 10/5, 1.805m on 10/26 (settlement price $8.11), a Top HoldCo tranche maturing 10/30, and a final V3 tranche on 11/30. Holdings after 10/26 were 52.9m direct (V3) plus Top HoldCo. This is mechanical, with the dealer pre-hedged, but the Form 4 for the 10/30 tranche lands around 11/3 as visible insider-supply headlines.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Earlier coverage attributed slides to 'insider-sale overhang' (rallies.ai). There is no measured print-day effect.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, since the dealer hedge was laid off in Nov 2025. Filed because it is a sourced overhang inside the window; sized near zero.
findings.independence: The 10/7 Form 4 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1819989/000112329226001381/form4.xml), the same filer and instrument.

findings.finding: Sector tape into the print is risk-off. On 10/30, finviz headlines include 'Crypto stocks drop after record $6.3bn Binance hack' (Investing.com) and 'Wall Street Is in Denial: AI Financing Problems Are Already Here, Barclays Strategist Warns' (Benzinga). AAII has CIFR at $7.075, -12.65%, intraday 10/30, against an October high of $16.42. Over a weekend gap, the hack's resolution or escalation moves crypto-linked equities on Monday in either direction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CIFR trades with crypto-equity and AI-infrastructure beta (peers fell 10-15% in the 10/8-10/15 week, per Trefis). Sector moves have dominated non-print days.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a macro-to-company proxy. The 10/30 drop already holds the first leg, and whether the hack story worsens or fades over the weekend is unknowable. Sized small, near-symmetric.
findings.independence: The finviz headline list for 10/30 (https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=CIFR). Web search could not independently confirm the Binance hack; treat it as single-sourced headlines.

outside_window.finding: The final V3 tranche of the Bitfury-group forward sale (1.805m pledged shares) matures 2026-11-30, and the company's 45-day lock-up from the 10-13 convert expires about late November. Both are possible supply events after the window.
Barber Lake halls 3-5 are scheduled to deliver Q4 2026 to Q1 2027, with rent ramping per hall. The confirmations land after the window.

baseline_tension: What I found agrees with the skew: calls are bid and the slight up-lean rests on a crowded short after a -53.6% run-down. Agreeing with the skew means it is probably mostly priced, so p_up sits only 4 points above 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 3/7 (own caveat reaches the number): positioning +1.5 cut to +1.0, because part of the 21.7-26.6% short interest is convert-arb hedging that does not cover on news.
Lesson 6 (inside what the company already told the market): Barber Lake slip -1.0 cut to -0.5. The phased schedule and overrun burden have been public since 9-25.
Lesson 6 / core table (pre-released period): pre-published KPI finding +0.5 cut to +0.2. abs_move came down from 18 to 17 as Q3 KPIs are known, partly offset by the chance of a new lease.
Lesson 1 (this name has not paid on the revenue line): revenue-bar finding -0.5 cut to -0.3. Q1 missed and rose 23.5%.

Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the answer was that it funds a contracted $9.1bn Barber Lake build, so it is signed positive-to-zero; the lock-up inference was still trimmed from +0.5 to +0.3 as an inference.
Lesson 5 (proxy smaller, not left out): lease-wave tail +1.5 cut to +1.0. The macro tape finding was kept at -0.3 as a proxy.
Lesson 2 (one-off below operating income): warrant gain left at +0.2-0.3 (+0.3 draft, +0.2 final); no path to the guide.
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): two estimate sources agree on revenue within 2%, so no global cap was applied. p_up moved from 55 to 54.
